name: Nancy Pelosi
role: U.S. Representative from California (1987-2027); Speaker of the House (2007-2011, 2019-2023)
summary: A San Francisco Democrat who led House Democrats for two decades, Pelosi is a mainstream liberal whose record centres on expanding health coverage, abortion and LGBTQ rights, gun regulation and climate investment. She works within capitalism, wanting stronger regulation, enforceable trade standards and taxes on corporations. On foreign policy she is a hawkish critic of China and a strong supporter of Israel and NATO, while she opposed the 2002 Iraq war authorization.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Helped pass the Affordable Care Act (voted Aye, 219-212) and says her aim is to expand coverage, but she has not endorsed Bernie Sanders's single-payer bill, so evidence for state-guaranteed coverage for everyone is mixed.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: As Speaker she spearheaded the Fair Minimum Wage Act of 2007, which raised the federal minimum wage.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Opposed the 2017 tax law as rewarding the rich and corporations; backed the Inflation Reduction Act's 15% corporate minimum tax and 1% stock-buyback tax, while promising no new taxes under $400,000.

unions-good.rationale: Her official page promotes federal investments that create 'good-paying union jobs', treating union employment as a goal of policy.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Voted for the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (2010) and backed a corporate minimum tax and buyback tax.

cut-welfare.rationale: Opposed the welfare overhauls proposed by President Bush and those passed under President Clinton.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Mixed record: voted for the 2001 Patriot Act, voted against reauthorizing certain provisions in 2005 (calling it a 'massive invasion of privacy'), and supported the PRISM program as of 2014.

limit-guns.rationale: Supports universal background checks, closing the 'Charleston loophole', safe storage and reinstating the assault-weapons and high-capacity magazine ban.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Voted against the Defense of Marriage Act in 1996, led House passage of the Respect for Marriage Act, and said in 2012 that her faith compels her to oppose bans on gay marriage as discrimination.

abortion-legal.rationale: Describes Dobbs as a disgraceful and devastating decision, calls abortion a woman's basic health decision, supports the Women's Health Protection Act, and voted against bans such as the 2003 partial-birth abortion ban.

more-religion-public.rationale: Voted in 1999 against displaying the Ten Commandments in public buildings including schools.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Describes immigration as central to American identity ('in diversity lies strength'), backs the Dream and Promise Act with a path to citizenship, and voted against the 2006 Secure Fence Act.

free-trade.rationale: Mixed: voted for NAFTA (1993) but against China PNTR (2000) and CAFTA (2005), opposed the Colombia deal, and demanded enforceable labor and environmental terms in USMCA.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Supported NATO's 1999 bombing of Yugoslavia, calling Kosovo a challenge to the conscience of the country, and backed the 2011 NATO intervention in Libya.

open-borders.rationale: Her official stance is for 'strong, smart border security' and she opposes a border wall, not for abolishing border controls.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Calls climate change 'the existential threat of our time' and led the Inflation Reduction Act ($370 billion for climate); in 2019 she dismissed the Green New Deal as written, so support is for large but not maximal action.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Backed the CHIPS and Science Act and IRA investment programs, which steer public funds into semiconductors and clean energy.

conscription.rationale: Said she did not support Charles Rangel's plan to reinstate the military draft.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Said in 2018 that there is 'no greater political accomplishment in the 20th Century than the establishment of the State of Israel' and called the U.S.-Israel bond 'unbreakable'.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Supported the 2009 Recovery Act stimulus package.

force-without-un.rationale: Mixed: in 2002 she urged respecting the UN and a multilateral approach on Iraq, but in 1999 she backed NATO's Kosovo campaign, which lacked Security Council approval.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Opposing the 1996 welfare law as a whole is nearby; work requirements not addressed separately.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Her record is on the side of civil-rights law: voted for the Civil Rights Restoration Act, backs the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act and the Equality Act.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Voted to strip a provision allowing oil and gas drilling in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge and blocked efforts to revive offshore drilling in protected areas.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Backs the Equality Act extending civil-rights protections to LGBTQ people and says the right to vote must be protected for all Americans.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Supports NATO: called its fate a vital national interest in 1999 and issued a statement on Finland and Sweden's NATO accession.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Reported to agree with the U.S. stance in support of land-for-peace in the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.

no-bailouts.rationale: As Speaker she voted for the 2008 Emergency Economic Stabilization Act (TARP), the bank rescue.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Insisted on 'no enforcement, no treaty' in the USMCA, demanding labor and environmental protections with strong enforcement, warning that without them workers would be 'locked into another bad deal'.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Supports the Equality Act banning discrimination against LGBTQ Americans in employment, housing, credit and public accommodations; the House passed it twice.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Moved the Robert E. Lee statue out of Statuary Hall, backed legislation to remove Confederate statues, and in 2020 ordered four paintings of Confederate Speakers taken down.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Strongly opposed President Bush's post-2004 plan to let workers direct part of their Social Security withholding into private accounts, and says Democrats will defend the program.

corporate-influence.rationale: Her page calls for ending 'dark money', stricter lobbying oversight and a constitutional amendment to overturn Citizens United, to stop 'unlimited, undisclosed spending by corporations and billionaires'.

non-intervention.rationale: Supported the 1999 NATO Kosovo campaign and the 2011 Libya intervention, rejecting a blanket ban on intervening in other states.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Says ending discrimination against gays and lesbians has been a top priority since her first day in Congress and speaks out for LGBTQ people persecuted in Uganda and Chechnya.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Supports the Equality Act's protections based on gender identity, opposed Trump's transgender military ban and Republican efforts targeting trans children.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Backs the NATO alliance and led a congressional delegation to Ukraine in 2022 to show support.

racial-franchise.rationale: Backs the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act and restoring Voting Rights Act protections against discrimination in voting.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Led the Democratic majority in repealing Don't Ask, Don't Tell and describes it as sent to the 'dustbin of history'.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Pledged in 2007 to bring the Armenian genocide resolution to a vote, saw it pass in 2019 (405-11), and reaffirmed recognition in 2026.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Supported NATO's Kosovo bombing and the Libya intervention, which were not responses to an attack on the U.S.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Voted against the 1995 balanced budget constitutional amendment.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Her page backs loan refinancing, public-service loan forgiveness and welcomes President Biden's student debt relief as 'historic'.

close-ties-china.rationale: Pressed a harder line on China throughout her career: opposed PNTR in 2000, backed a currency-manipulator bill, and visited Taiwan in 2022 to stress that America stands with Taiwan.

notes: On stock trading she said in Dec 2024 that the House is a free-market economy, but in July 2025 she told CNN she very much supports a ban on trading by members of Congress; no statement in the list covers it directly. Votes on the 2002 Iraq war (against, source s19) and Tiananmen-era China trade policy are recorded but no statement matches the exact wording. Announced in November 2025 she would not seek re-election in 2026.
